paper_metadata.title: LLM-Guided Ans¨atze Design for Quantum Circuit Born Machines in Financial Generative Modeling

summary: The paper presents a 12-qubit QCBM for financial generative modeling of JGB interest-rate time series, using an LLM-generated ansatz that reaches depth 28 versus 85 for the TwoLocal baseline. Quantitatively, the LLM ansatz attains KL divergence 3.67 on the noiseless simulator and 7.37 ± 0.11 on ibm_fez without error mitigation, but the TwoLocal baseline is better on the reported KL metric in both simulator (3.10) and hardware (9.32 ± 0.06 without EM, 8.92 ± 0.07 with EM).

experiments.description: LLM-generated QCBM ansatz for financial generative modeling of Japanese Government Bond (JGB) interest-rate time series, evaluated on noiseless Qiskit Aer simulator and on real IBM quantum hardware, compared against a TwoLocal baseline.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM) with LLM-generated hardware-aware ansatz
algorithm.convergence_criteria: 30 training epochs on simulator; extended training typically 50 to 100 epochs mentioned for convergence analysis
algorithm.parameter_initialization: LLM-generated circuit architecture initialized from hardware-aware prompt; parameter initialization not specified

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Real-valued JGB interest-rate changes are uniformly quantized into binary strings; 4 qubits allocated per maturity (5, 10, 20 years), totaling 12 qubits
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize MMD loss during training; evaluate generative fit using reverse KL divergence D_KL(Q || P) between model distribution Q and data distribution P
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hardware-aware prompt engineering to satisfy qubit connectivity and native basis-gate constraints; validity flag used; post-selection and measurement error mitigation used in analysis

problem_instance.description: Generative modeling of daily changes in Japanese Government Bond interest rates across three maturities

dataset_specification.description: Daily rates for 5-, 10-, and 20-year maturities from 2000-01-04 to 2025-02-28; 4 qubits per maturity; 12 qubits total

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Uniform binning / fixed-bit binary encoding of real-valued rates using min-max scaling to n-bit representation
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Training on simulator with 10,000 shots per circuit evaluation; comparison of LLM-generated ansatz vs TwoLocal baseline; real-device evaluation with and without measurement error mitigation; post-selection analysis on valid bitstrings

noise_model.error_mitigation_method: Measurement error mitigation (Mthree) on real hardware; post-selection
noise_model.mitigation_details: Measurement error mitigation via Mthree; post-selection on valid bitstrings

implementation_details.transpilation_target: ibm_fez basis gates / hardware-aware no-transpilation execution
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Min-max scaling and uniform quantization to binary strings
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Reverse KL divergence computation; measurement error mitigation; post-selection on valid bitstrings

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: MMD loss converges around 0.006 over 15 epochs in figure caption

speedup_claims.conditions: The paper reports better hardware efficiency and lower circuit depth for the LLM-generated ansatz, but does not claim an asymptotic or formal speedup.
speedup_claims.caveats: Performance is discussed in terms of shallower circuits and improved noise resilience on real hardware, not computational speedup.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 12-qubit IBM ibm_fez execution with 10,000 shots per circuit evaluation; LLM-generated ansatz depth 28 versus TwoLocal depth 85.
limiting_factors: TwoLocal baseline achieves lower KL divergence on the noiseless simulator (3.10 vs 3.67).
On real hardware, the baseline also outperforms the LLM-generated circuit both without EM (9.32 vs 7.37) and with EM (8.92 vs 6.91), so the quantum method is not better on the reported metric.
No asymptotic or constant-factor quantum speedup is claimed or demonstrated.
Performance gains are limited to circuit depth reduction and noise resilience, not computational advantage.

notes: hardware.type set to simulator_other for aer_simulator and real_qpu_superconducting for ibm_fez is reflected in the experiment description; the hardware block records the primary simulator run, while the paper also reports real-device execution on IBM ibm_fez.
qubit_type inferred as physical for ibm_fez execution; the paper explicitly says the circuit is executed on real IBM quantum hardware using 12 qubits.
speedup_order is none_proven because the paper discusses practical performance and hardware efficiency but does not claim or characterize an asymptotic quantum speedup.
The paper emphasizes hardware-aware ansatz design and improved depth/noise robustness, but the classical TwoLocal baseline is better on KL divergence in both simulator and hardware results.
